plain.text: God blessed Noah and his sons: "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth." Animals would fear them. God gave them every living creature for food, as he had given green plants, but they must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it. God would demand an accounting for human life, because God made mankind in his own image.

God made a covenant with Noah, his descendants and every living creature: never again would a flood destroy all life on the earth. "I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth." Whenever the rainbow appears, God will remember his everlasting covenant.

Noah's sons were Shem, Ham (the father of Canaan) and Japheth. Noah planted a vineyard, drank some of its wine, became drunk and lay uncovered in his tent. Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers. Shem and Japheth walked in backwards with a garment and covered their father without looking. When Noah woke and learned what Ham had done, he cursed Ham's son Canaan, saying he would be a servant to his brothers.
Noah blessed the LORD, the God of Shem, and asked that God would extend Japheth's territory. Noah lived 350 years after the flood and died at 950 years old.

summary.bigIdea: God makes a covenant with all life on earth, with the rainbow as its sign, but human weakness continues.
points: God blesses Noah's family and says human life is precious because people bear God's image.
The rainbow is a sign of God's promise never again to destroy the earth by flood.
Noah gets drunk, showing that even after a fresh start, people still fail.
summary.reflection: Next time you see a rainbow, what promise of God could it remind you of?
